Playback settings

Applies to this section and all its paths when entering step view. Off by default; plays every 3 seconds when on. The editor preview always starts paused.

Select a beat to edit it or branch after it. Step content is shared by paths that reference it. Append, duplicate and move affect the selected path; deleting a step removes it everywhere. Copies repeat patches, including appended events. Reveal/hide indices stay positional within each path.

Honeycomb trace → diagram

Paste event JSON or open an export, preview its size, then choose all exported spans or a focused branch. Conversion runs locally. Build diagram replaces the editor in one undo step.

Custom field names

Default fields: trace.trace_id, trace.span_id, trace.parent_id, service.name, name, timestamp, duration_ms, error. Override only the fields that differ. Time is ISO with timezone or Unix seconds; duration is milliseconds.

Focus keeps exported descendants so included spans retain child timing. Parent IDs at the boundary remain unchanged.

      Contracts & page structure

      Authoring contract

      Hand this block to an agent along with the HLD, code, or docs it should diagram. The output drops straight into the engine. Hand-editing works the same way; validation errors name the field and say what to fix. The full contract lives in contract/authoring-contract.md.

      
    
      

    
      Schema reference
      
    
      Everything optional has a default. Unknown fields are
    ignored, never fatal. A bare diagram object (just nodes + rows) is
    accepted and wrapped in a one-section page; page.sections (no tabs) still works
    unchanged.
      
    
      
    
      
      
      keyshapemeaning
      
      
      page{title, skin?, protocols?, lanes?, blocks}The whole doc page. skin: aurora daylight editorial terminal pastel blueprint (pastel default). sections is accepted as an alias for a blocks list with no tabs.
      
      
      page.blocks[n]section | {tabs:[...]}Ordered content. A block is either a section object (below) or a tabs container.
      
      
      tabs[n]{label, sections:[...]}One tab: a label and its sections. All tabs render; inactive panels are hidden (their ambient animation stops painting). Arrow keys move between tabs.
      
      
      page.protocols{kind: {label, color}}Extends the built-in kind table (https, int, mqtt). color is one hex, or {aurora, daylight}. Edges, packets, arrowheads, and the legend all read this one table, so they cannot drift.
      
      
      page.lanes{LANE: {color, label?}}Declares step lanes (e.g. NET / DEV / CAM). A step tagged lane shows a colored pill on its caption line.
      
      
      sections[n]{heading?, accent?, source?, text?, bullets?, contract?, diagram?}One bounding box. accent: green blue violet amber pink cyan red slate or a hex; defaults cycle. text is a paragraph or list of paragraphs. source: optional permalink (HLD section) — renders a small "source↗" chip beside the heading, new tab.
      
      
      sections[n].contract{title?, source?, fields:[{k, v?, g?, hot?, link?, delta?, revealAt?, hideAt?}], note?}Message-contract card: a compact "on the wire" field table. delta is added|removed|changed; reveal indices bind the row to this section's diagram steps. Optional source chip on the card title and footer note.
      
      
      diagram.view"ambient" | "step" | "ambient-only"How the board opens. ambient (default): live view with an AMBIENT/STEP toggle when steps exist. step: opens as the click-through at step 1. ambient-only: no toggle — for boards without a meaningful sequence. One diagram spec always drives both flavors.
      
      
      diagram.autoplaybooleanDefaults to false: step view opens paused. Set true to advance every 3 seconds when step view opens. Workbench and Confluence configuration previews stay paused; reduced motion disables automatic steps. No schema-version change needed.
      
      
      diagram.nodes{id: {title?, sub?, icon?, tint?, group?, link?}}Service cards. icon from the shared library (default gear); use Browse icons to search names or filter categories; tint colors the icon chip (default cmd). group: containment-boundary membership. link: optional permalink — a small clickable ↗ on the card corner, new tab.
      
      
      diagram.groups{groupId: {title?}}Declares containment boundaries: a dashed titled box drawn around all member nodes (a device holding two chips). Put members in one stack column; an edge between stack members draws as a vertical interconnect.
      
      
      diagram.rows[[slot, ...], ...]Slots render left to right in every row. A slot is a node id, or an array of ids = a stack (members render top to bottom in one column). Cross-row edges follow their endpoint positions.
      
      
      diagram.routing"curves" | "lanes"Optional lane routing reserves tracks and ports around cards. Supports 1–5 unstacked cards per row, no floats or self-loops; otherwise warns and uses curves. New diagrams, catalog seeds, trace imports and built-in template projects default to no lanes. Select the section heading, then Inspect → Edge routing to switch. Readable size enlarges the board for horizontal scrolling.
      
      
      diagram.floats[{id, side:"above", x?, y?}]Nodes outside the rows. Without coordinates, above/below placement is automatic. Both x and y pin the center in diagram units. Drag any float to pin it; use inspector Float X/Y for precision or choose Auto above/below to release it. Row nodes keep their row/slot gestures.
      
      
      diagram.edges{from, to, kind?, ret?, label?, fromPort?, toPort?, bend?, labelDx?, labelDy?, revealAt?, hideAt?}kind is the protocol (default int). Optional ports are {side:"top|right|bottom|left",offset:0.5}, with offset 0–1 along the side. Inspector Exit/Entry side and position (%) pin endpoints; Auto restores routing. Pinned edges use curves even in lane layouts. Zero-based reveal indices draw the edge only for the selected step interval; bend/label offsets tune geometry.
      
      
      diagram.sectionLayout{default:[{x:0,y:0,w:8,h:12},{panel:"home",x:8,y:0,w:4,h:12}]}Saved twelve-column tile layouts: default, backstage, confluence. Use controls:"steps" for a movable playback/path/caption tile. Arrange section to drag/resize; Preview selects the target and Optimize layout supplies a starting arrangement. Coordinates are zero-based, height 3–40 rows. Unspecified tiles stay visible; narrow views stack. Layout guide.
      
      
      diagram.primaryPanel"home"Optional centerpiece panel ID: show it large with playback below it and a collapsible Data flow underneath. Set Presentation → Centerpiece in the panel inspector. Homemap steps have device states, subject drag/tap placement, visibility, inheritance, and signal controls.
      
      
      diagram.brand{app?, icon?, logo?, logoImage?, accent?, bg?, fg?}Shared company branding for Phone, Device app, Camera screen and Security monitoring. Select a panel, then open Company branding to edit shared settings, override this panel or hide its brand. panel.brand inherits when absent, suppresses with false, and overrides with a partial object. Choose a library icon, 1–4 character monogram, or upload an embedded PNG/JPEG/WebP up to 512 KiB. Colors use #RGB or #RRGGBB.
      
      
      diagram.panels[{id, type, title?, ...}]Synchronized inspector widgets beside the board. Panel types are documented in contract/authoring-contract.md, including static embedded image references, table for data snapshots, checks for authored decisions, budget for resource limits, and replicas for positions and reported lag. waterfall supports startMs offsets for overlapping trace spans; trace shows service internals and child-covered versus uncovered wall time.
      
      
      steps[n].id"ota.3"Optional unique step identifier for deep links, search and preview restoration. Duplicating a step gives its copy a new ID.
      
      
      diagram.paths[{id, label?, color?, steps:[step IDs]}]Optional named outcomes sharing one step registry and board. First path is the default. Chips start paths at step 1. Shared beginnings use clickable shadows; consecutive shared IDs after divergence form a common track. Paths can split and rejoin again. Shared ending means all participating paths finish there; early endings never connect to later blocks they do not visit. Full authored sequences determine blocks, including hidden stops. Numbers, playback and state follow the selected participating path. Shared circles keep it when possible and identify the participating path otherwise. Conflicting shared orders retain separate occurrences with sharing cues. No path label unless alternates exist. Story steps can fork, rename, recolor and remove paths.
      
      
      diagram.steps[{edge | edges, nodes?, panels?, lane?, text, link?}]Ordered narrative. edge:"from->to" or edges:[...] for hops that happen together — their packets fire in order, staggered. A step may be edgeless: light nodes:[...] directly and/or patch panels. panels carries SPARSE per-panel patches; the engine folds them into complete per-step state so any jump is consistent (log appends; enterOnce applies only at its own step). Drives the numbered coins, the ambient packet schedule, AND the click-through.
      
      
      step.failures{"from->to":"dropped" | "blocked"}Current-step communication outcomes. Dropped packets stop at an orange break and fade; blocked communications show a stop marker without sending. Failed hops override normal packets and focus only their source unless nodes explicitly select the destination. Static markers remain with reduced motion. Edit with each hop’s Delivery selector or Add failed communication.
      
      
      iconsUse Browse icons for the shared library across nodes, groups, Home elements, Device app cards and company marks. Categories include Power, Temperature, Security, Connectivity, Audio and Dispatch; examples: battery-full battery-low battery-charging hot cold armed disarmed triggered camera wifi headset. Icon IDs and recipe.
      
      
      tintscmd auth data mqtt dev
      
      
      scenesperson-at-door-night person-through-door doorbell-run-away doorbell-runners package-drop kitchen-fire static-noise (stock scenes for the screen widget)
      
    
      
    
      

    
      Reserved fields (forward-compatible, not yet rendered)
      
    
      Shaped now so richer renderers can add them without
    breaking existing specs. Today's engine tolerates and ignores them.
      
    
      
    
      
      
      keyshapemeaning
      
      
      steps[n].stickytrue | falseExplicit persistence flag for board effects across steps (panel state already persists via patch folding).
      
    
      
    
      

    
      
      
      Handles well
        
        
          
      • Tabbed multi-section pages from one JSON — diagrams and click-throughs side by side
        • 
          
      • One diagram spec, both flavors: ambient + step playback from the same steps
        • 
          
      • Synchronized inspector panels: state machines, LEDs, gauges, logs, camera screen — sparse patches folded to complete per-step state
        • 
          
      • Containment groups (a device boundary around chips) with vertical stack interconnects
        • 
          
      • Left-to-right rows with 3–5 slots; stacks of 2–4; automatic or freely positioned floats
        • 
          
      • Legend, edges, packets, and arrowheads all from the one protocol table
        • 
        
      
      
      
      
      Known limits (by design, for now)
        
        
          
      • Automatic avoidance is best-effort; crowded corridors may need ports, bend or label nudges
        • 
          
      • Hidden tabs stop painting, but SMIL clocks keep running — ambient dots are mid-path when a tab is revealed (harmless for loops)
        • 
          
      • Switching tabs pauses a click-through. In this workbench, use Play to resume from the same step.
        • 
          
      • Freely placed nodes can overlap; choose their positions and check the resulting connections
        • 
          
      • Group members must be placed adjacently (one stack column works best); the boundary is a bounding box, not a layout constraint
        •
